author: Mark Atwood
text:
Idiom rating (second rusty pass): CLEAN — the prior /review-rusty pass already covered the substantive idiom issues in request.rs / blob.rs / client.rs (.47–.54). This second pass scanned the files less covered by the prior pass (auth.rs, sse.rs, ws/mod.rs, push.rs, benches/session_and_urls.rs, examples/session_fetch.rs, tests/common/log_capture.rs, tests/log_redaction.rs, tests/client_tests.rs). Net new findings: 2 — both clippy-level (.55 format-push-string in bench loop, .56 positional format args in bench file inconsistent with the 71e9bb2 inline-args sweep). Both are P3, both are bench-file-only. No new unsafe issues, no new error-handling issues, no new ownership issues, no new lifetime issues, no new trait-shape issues. The src/ tree is squarely idiomatic Rust 2024.

Rust idiom confidence (second pass): ~10% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: none — both new findings are mechanical clippy-grade. Uncertainty driven by: (a) not running `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` to confirm both findings actually fire under the current lint config (the workspace pre-commit gate runs `--workspace` but I did not verify it includes `--all-targets` to pick up benches); (b) not running `cargo +nightly clippy -p jmap-base-client --benches -- -W clippy::pedantic` to surface the long-tail pedantic flags on the bench file. Would raise confidence if: (1) ran the workspace pre-commit gate green; (2) ran `cargo clippy --benches` specifically on jmap-base-client; (3) checked whether any sibling *-client crate has already replicated the bench pattern (and thus would need the same sweep).

Bikeshedding flag: 0 — both findings have engineering basis (clippy::format_push_string allocates per-iter; clippy::uninlined_format_args inconsistent with the recent 71e9bb2 workspace sweep). Neither is opinion.
